name: Fable Barbell
strategy: Cross-sectional sector-momentum long/short: long the top-5 non-AI momentum ETFs vs short the bottom-3 broken downtrends, correlation-deduped, with hard stop/take-profit discipline, re-ranked weekly.

positions.thesis: Top momentum rank retained: +~25% YTD on the $106B biotech M&A wave; trimmed one point for this week's wobble, and falling rates help the long-duration biotech trade.
Strongest confirmation in the book: ~4% off all-time highs at $76, and the dovish shift adds a bull-steepener to the existing net-interest-income tailwind.
Fuel-cost windfall intact as the oil war premium deflates toward sub-$80 WTI; jobs contraction is a demand-risk watch item, so held rather than added.
Industrials keep sector leadership with cheaper energy inputs and now cheaper capital; survives the dedupe as the broader, less freight-levered of the XLI/IYT pair.

New fifth long, switched from the short side by the re-rank: confirmed breakout over the descending trendline (~$90) on the strongest short-lookback momentum in the universe, driven by falling real yields and gold above $4,300; targets $95-105.

Bottom rank: worst-performing sector YTD on weak fundamentals and low consumer confidence, and July's outright job losses hit discretionary spending first; stop guards against a rate-cut-relief rally.
Broken uptrend: 2026's gains were the Iran war premium, which keeps evaporating (WTI low-$80s, EIA sub-$80 Q3); flipping last month's exited long to a short as the catalyst unwinds.
Bottom-3 rank: -24.8% YTD in a persistent downtrend with no reversal catalyst; smallest weight of the sleeve for its liquidity and squeeze risk.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Weekly re-rank forced by a regime break, not churn: the book already lost GDXJ and URNM shorts to stops this week, and the surviving SLV short sits ~1% from its stop with silver +11% on a macro catalyst (payrolls -23k, hike odds collapsing) — I cover it deliberately rather than donate the last point to the squeeze. The metals complex flipped from bottom-rank shorts to top-rank momentum, so the mandate says switch sides: GDX enters as a LONG (breakout over its downtrend line at ~$90 with falling real yields behind it and targets $95-105). IYT exits because it is a correlation-duplicate of XLI (mandate requires dedupe) and its freight exposure is the long most damaged by an outright jobs contraction. New bottom-3 shorts are the actual broken downtrends now: XLY (worst YTD sector, weak consumer confidence, now negative payrolls), XOP (its entire 2026 trend was the war premium, which keeps deflating with WTI low-$80s heading sub-$80), and MSOS (-24.8% YTD, no reversal catalyst). After watching shorts get massacred across the experiment (12 of 17 fired orders), I run the short sleeve at 14% instead of 18% with -12% stops and +20% TPs — the re-rank keeps the mandate's structure while cutting the squeeze surface.
novelty: Novelty vs my Round-2 barbell: zero symbol overlap in either direction — this book expresses the dovish turn cross-sectionally (long GDX miners momentum vs short XLY/XOP/MSOS laggards) rather than through Round 2's buy-and-hedge quality/AI barbell, and its only metals exposure is leveraged miner equity momentum, not Round 2's GLD ballast.
research_notes: Checked: (1) Macro — July nonfarm payrolls -23k vs +80k expected, first outright decline, with -103k revisions; unemployment 4.1%; Sept hike odds fell 57%->~44%; Treasuries rallied, dollar hit a two-week low. (2) Tape — S&P 500 record close 7,757 (+3.6% wk), Nasdaq +5.2%, SOXX +7% wk (semi-short squeeze confirmed), software/IGV +10% since July while still -24.3% YTD. (3) Metals — gold above $4,300 (+7.5% wk), silver ~$64 (+11% wk, 6-week high), GDX ~$89.86 with a confirmed breakout over its descending trendline and technician targets $95-105; my SLV short is within ~1% of its -12% stop with its downtrend thesis invalidated. (4) ANET Q2 (Aug 4): $3.04B rev (first $3B quarter), EPS $1.02 vs $0.90, third FY26 guide raise to $12.6B, stock +12% AH — validates the AI-networking leg. (5) KRE ~$76, ~4% below all-time high; regional banks get a bull-steepener from the dovish shift. (6) Oil — WTI low-$80s, war premium still deflating, EIA sub-$80 Q3 view intact; XOP badly lagging OIH. (7) XLY = worst YTD sector (weak consumer confidence, now a jobs contraction); MSOS -24.8% YTD. (8) BTC ~$64.9k, +4.6% since Monday, +9.8% July, supported by falling yields/ETF inflows — the dovish catalyst my cut perp leg was waiting for. Lesson applied: 12 of 17 fired standing orders in this experiment were miner/semi shorts stopped out; both my remaining shorts (SOXL, SLV) were built for a hawkish regime that ended Friday.
